title: Stream-aware span wrapping for tool calls with deterministic redaction
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Add a streaming-observability feature that wraps tracing spans across chunk boundaries for requests that invoke tools/function calls, while ensuring deterministic, grammar-aware redaction of streamed content and backward-compatible trace propagation for older SDKs. This ticket covers design, implementation, tests, and rollout plan for per-chunk annotations that link chunks to the original tool call and the final structured output. It must maintain latency SLOs and preserve provenance for post-hoc audits.
acceptance_criteria: Per-chunk telemetry includes: chunk_index, parent_tool_call_id, span_id, chunk_latency_ms, and redact_status
Tracing spans are created and closed deterministically for requests with interleaved tool/function calls across streamed chunks
Redaction pipeline produces identical scrubbed output regardless of chunk boundaries (idempotent scrubber), with configurable grammar rules and allowlists
SDK compatibility layer forwards trace context for older SDKs that do not set trace headers, without changing public API surface
End-to-end tests validate trace linking across chunk boundaries and replayability for audit logs
P99 latency increase for streaming paths is < 8% for default batching profile
Documentation and console surfaces (per-route telemetry) updated with examples and troubleshooting steps
implementation_notes: Introduce a lightweight chunk header that includes parent_tool_call_id and sequence_id; serialize as base64 to avoid protocol changes
Wrap tracing spans at the tool-call level and emit 'slice' spans for each chunk that inherit trace_id and set slice_index attribute
Integrate grammar-aware scrubber (existing pipeline) and add a deterministic tokenization step to ensure identical redaction across differently sized chunks
Provide a fallback in the router: if trace headers absent, the compatibility shim will generate a stable trace_id derived from request nonce and route hash
Add feature flag to enable controlled rollout and a sampling knob for per-chunk detailed telemetry
Measure overhead in nightly perf job and add a microbenchmark for chunk header parsing and span creation
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Additional per-chunk metadata increases network/ingestion volume. Mitigation: compress header and sample verbose fields; use telemetry sampling for high-throughput customers.
Risk: Redaction discrepancies when downstream transforms re-chunk. Mitigation: include canonicalized tokenization and canonical redact logs to compare post-hoc.
Risk: Older SDKs may break binary compatibility if headers are enforced. Mitigation: implement compatibility shim in gateway layer and document SDK upgrade path.
Risk: Increased span cardinality may stress tracing backend. Mitigation: attach low-cardinality attributes and use span sampling for non-critical flows.
test_plan: Unit tests for chunk header encoding/decoding
Integration tests: simulate tool calls that emit multi-chunk streams and verify span linkage and per-chunk telemetry
Property tests for redaction idempotency: split inputs at random boundaries and assert identical scrubbed outputs
Perf regression test gating: run against baseline with representative workloads and assert <8% P99 latency regression
Canary rollout: enable for 5% of customers with advanced telemetry and monitor error/latency/cost metrics
